mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to the prior 6-month average compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days. This mechanism operates continuously without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS change and SPX return is below 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% over 3 months, it signals economic contraction that triggers immediate equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400.0 and consumer spending (RSAFS) below 690000.0 indicate weakening demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect correlation is below 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% sustained for 3 months), rising discount rates suppress equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 index level signals robust manufacturing output, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1400.0 thousand units, it indicates housing market weakness that reduces consumer confidence and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when HOUST is below 1400.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) above 156000.0 and declines in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.7% signal a tight labor market that fuels wage inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition occurs but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect correlation is below 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), overheating concerns trigger monetary tightening that produces negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition holds but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
